published_failure_contract: The target test hard-codes junit-4.13.1.jar in ManifestProperty annotations, so replacing the dependency removes the named artifact from the test class path.

source_isolation.evidence: JUnit release commit 05fe2a64 fixes the published artifact version at 4.13.2; the target test names junit-4.13.1.jar literally. This is an artifact-name contract, not a JUnit execution-behavior regression.

a1_input.evidence: The FSE workbook omits the target revision. The complete target history stops before JUnit 4.13.2 and contains no historical commit that runs this target with 4.13.2.

target_history.evidence: All 248 commits reachable from remote refs and 62 unique POM blobs were inspected. Eight POM blobs use 4.13.1, none uses 4.13.2, and the repository ended on 2020-11-15 before the 4.13.2 release. No maintainer changed the hard-coded artifact name for 4.13.2.

stop_reason: The deterministic artifact-name failure has no maintainer-authored A2; editing the annotation to the new filename would be a synthetic recovery.

Another module records the same signature after an ApacheDS replacement. The excerpt does not isolate any JUnit 4.13.2 behavior.

target_history.evidence: All 369 commits reachable from remote refs and 153 unique POM blobs were inspected. Three POM blobs use 4.13.1, none uses 4.13.2. The repository is archived and its final code activity was 2021-04-28.

stop_reason: The published failure is a dependency-independent signed-JAR failure and the target history contains no 4.13.2 repair.

published_failure_contract: An asynchronous subscription test reaches Mockito verification before shardConsumer.handleInput is observed.

source_isolation.evidence: The failing method is a plain @Test with no JUnit timeout, assumption serialization, or floating-point assertion. JUnit 4.13.2 changes those mechanisms, while the client failure occurs in its own executor-startup race. No release commit was found on the observed path.

a1_input.evidence: Pull request 879 preserves a historical step from c872cab0 to 8084281e that changes only the two JUnit declarations from 4.13.1 to 4.13.2. The FSE workbook omits its executed target revision, so this cannot be asserted as the workbook's exact checkout.

target_history.evidence: Maintainer PR 1084, commit b8d3390b, changes only ShardConsumerSubscriberTest, keeps JUnit 4.13.2 on both sides, and adds a wait so subscriptions start before verification. Its title and commit message explicitly call the tests flaky. It repairs the client race but does not identify a JUnit-induced regression.

stop_reason: A precise target race repair exists, but no precise JUnit source mechanism causes the failure. Replaying it as a JUnit impact case would relabel an acknowledged flaky test as an upstream breakage.
